🇲🇽🐉 Mexico won't rush the USMCA review just to please Washington

The July 1 deadline lands this week — and Washington itself now projects the review will run past it. After a second bilateral round in June on agriculture and energy, a third round is set for the week of July 20 in Mexico City. No signatures forced by a calendar.

The US is pushing stricter rules of origin to wall Chinese content out of North American supply chains. Mexico has already moved on its own terms: tariffs on more than 1,400 products from non-FTA countries, plus 52 US trade demands on the table. But Ebrard's message is "no rush" — Mexico won't accept terms that compromise the national interest just to hit a date.

That's the sovereign read. China sells Mexico roughly $130B a year — much of it intermediate goods Mexican plants turn into exports — against about $10B flowing back. Diversification isn't picking a side; it's refusing to let any partner set your clock. 🇲🇽

🇲🇽🌎 "Our relationship with the United States must be built on recognition of each nation's sovereignty." "Nuestra relación con los Estados Unidos debe seguir construyéndose sobre principios muy claros: el respeto mutuo, el diálogo, la cooperación, y el reconocimiento de la soberanía de cada nación." "Our relationship with the United States must keep being built on very clear principles: mutual respect, dialogue, cooperation, and recognition of each nation's sovereignty." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Metapa, Chiapas Said with US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and US Ambassador Ronald Johnson present. The plant targets the screwworm, a pest that crosses borders. As Sheinbaum put it: animal diseases and plagues "know no borders" — the answer is shared capacity, not confrontation.

🇲🇽🏭 A strategic plant built in 12 months — by a Mexican institution. "Senasica —una institución que es un orgullo nacional— hizo realidad esta Planta en 12 meses... talento y corazón mexicanos con cooperación estadounidense." "Senasica — an institution that is a national pride — made this plant a reality in 12 months... Mexican talent and heart, with US cooperation." — Julio Berdegué, Mexico's agri-food coordinator, Metapa, Chiapas Mexico's first screwworm case appeared in November 2024. Until now, all of North and Central America depended on a single sterile-fly plant in Pacora, Panama. The new Metapa plant restores the region's own production capacity — built by Mexico's Senasica in 12 months.

🇲🇽🌎 "Cooperation between sovereign nations will always be more powerful than confrontation." "La cooperación entre países soberanos siempre será más poderosa que la confrontación, cuando se trata de proteger el bienestar de nuestros pueblos." "Cooperation between sovereign nations will always be more powerful than confrontation, when it comes to protecting the well-being of our peoples." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, inauguration of the binational sterile-fly plant, Metapa, Chiapas Mexico and the US jointly inaugurated a sterile-fly plant in Chiapas to eradicate the cattle screwworm. US Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins attended. Sheinbaum set the terms of the relationship: "mutual respect, dialogue, cooperation, and recognition of each nation's sovereignty."

🇲🇽📈 <u>MEXICO'S ECONOMY JUST POSTED ITS STRONGEST MONTH SINCE 2021</u>

Despite Trump's tariff threats and the T-MEC noise, Mexico's economy grew 2.2% year-on-year in April and 1.2% over March — the biggest monthly jump since 2021, more than doubling the 1.0% analysts forecast (Inegi). Construction surged 10.4% and farm output rose 4.4%. The 'Mexico is collapsing' narrative keeps colliding with the data.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>A POWERFUL MAN BEAT HIS WIFE ON CAMERA. HIS NEW GOVERNMENT POST WAS GONE WITHIN HOURS.</u>

After María Felicia Jiménez posted video of former Pemex director Víctor Rodríguez Padilla hitting, shoving and pulling her hair in front of their children, his pending appointment to lead the national clean-energy institute (INEEL) was cancelled. The Women's Secretariat: 'any act of violence against a woman must be addressed, investigated and sanctioned.' President Sheinbaum personally pledged support to the victim. No name is too connected.

🇲🇽🚆 <u>MEXICO IS BUILDING WITHOUT BORROWING — AND IT'S ABOUT TO SHOW UP IN THE GDP</u>

From July, Mexico's public-works boom starts registering in the GDP figures, Sheinbaum says — 750 billion pesos channeled into railways alone this term, all without taking on new debt. Neoliberal dogma always insisted you can't build big without borrowing big from the markets. Mexico is laying track, highways and housing and keeping the books clean at the same time.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>PAN'S TAMAULIPAS MACHINE: ~985 MILLION PESOS LOOTED FROM FOOD AID FOR THE POOR</u>

A former welfare secretary under PAN governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca was charged this week over the diversion of nearly 985 million pesos — money budgeted for despensas (food baskets) for Tamaulipas's poorest families. She's the second official from that administration to be prosecuted; a court ordered preventive detention but she dodged it with an injunction. This is the neoliberal 'social spending' model the 4T inherited: aid for the poor treated as a private piggy bank.

HOUSTON PUBLIC MEDIA: Trump signals he may pull out of trade agreement with Mexico and Canada, which could impact Texas businesses

June 23, 2026 | 🟢

📰 A US outlet names the actual threat to North American trade — not Mexico, but Trump, who now says "we do better as a country if we don't have an agreement," the same deal he once called "the fairest... we have ever signed."

🇲🇽 Texas has been the top US exporting state for 22 straight years with Mexico as its #1 partner; energy exports south topped $34 billion in 2024.

• Trump: "I would rather not have the agreement... we do better as a country if we don't have an agreement"
• Trade lawyer Michelle Schulz: "It would cause a great deal more disruption than the tariffs have already caused"

June 25, 2026 | 🟡

📰 A driver surrounded by celebrating fans in Cabo San Lucas accelerated into the crowd after Mexico beat Czechia 3-0 — a chaotic street-party incident, with the driver arrested. No cartel, no organized crime.
